title: Shortest Cycle in a Graph
summary: Given a bi-directional graph with n vertices labeled from 0 to n-1 , where the edges are represented by a 2D integer array, determine the length of the shortest cycle in the graph.
statement: Given a bi-directional graph with n vertices labeled from 0 to n-1 , where the edges are represented by a 2D integer array, determine the length of the shortest cycle in the graph. If no cycle exists, return -1. A cycle is defined as a path that starts and ends at the same node, with each edge in the path used exactly once.
constraints: Vertices are numbered zero through n-1 and edges are distinct undirected pairs.
Return the number of edges in the shortest simple cycle.
Return -1 when the graph contains no cycle.
hints: Run breadth-first search from every vertex.
Store each discovered node's distance and BFS parent.
An edge to a visited non-parent neighbor closes a cycle of the two distances plus one.
Every shortest cycle is exposed by a BFS rooted on it, while parent checks exclude immediate backtracking edges.
editorial: Every shortest cycle is exposed by a BFS rooted on it, while parent checks exclude immediate backtracking edges.

tests.explanation: The triangle among zero, one, and two is the shortest cycle, of length three.
This path has no cycle, so the result is negative one.
